mods.name: Ceramics
mods.description: Mod adding additional early game and vanilla-like tools made of clay. Includes fluid transport, decoration, and ceramic tools.

releases.notes:
Ported the mod to 1.21.

This release was create in parallel to [1.8.1 for 1.20.1](https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/releases/tag/v1.8.1). Any changes included in both releases are listed only on the changelog for 1.8.1.

## General

* Added tag translations.

## Fluids

* Ceramics now activates Mantle's potion fluid, powder snow fluid, honey fluid, and soup fluids, along with NeoForge's milk fluid.
  * This means the vanilla bowl, bottle, and bucket items all will be able to be dumped into cisterns, even if you lack another mod like Tinkers' providing such fluids.
* Ceramics now activates Mantle's fluid transfer JEI tab, adding cisterns as a catalyst.
* Powder Snow is now identified with the correct name `c:powder_snow` instead of the previous typo `powdered_snow`.
* Buckets now use NeoForge's cauldron fluid registry to fill and empty all mod added cauldrons automatically.
* Migrated to new NeoForge capabilities. Some fluid logic will be more performant.
* Fluid rendering now uses entity render types instead of a custom Mantle render type.
  * The most notable change is we use a non-transparent render type for fluids not marked as transparent, which should be more performant.
  * Cisterns now render fluids with the backfaces, so you will see the fluid when inside a cistern. 

## Recipes

* Added crackable ingredient, which matches crackable items with a particular range of cracks. Used to match uncracked items in some of our recipes.
* Removed no NBT ingredient.
* Moved all common tags to `c` tags instead of `forge`

## Models

* Simplified some model JSON using a few new template models.
* Bucket model no longer has the contents area inset.
* Removed `ceramics:fluid_bucket_model` in favor of Mantle's `mantle:fluid_container`. Notably now supports an override so water buckets are more vibrant.
* Reworked `ceramics:solid_bucket_model`. Now supports overrides for specific block contents, which we use to give powder snow a unique texture.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/compare/v1.8.1...v1.9.0

mods.name: Ceramics
mods.description: Mod adding additional early game and vanilla-like tools made of clay. Includes fluid transport, decoration, and ceramic tools.

releases.notes:
## Buckets

* Show creator mod ID for clay buckets, helping identify the mod that added a fluid.
* Powder snow when placed into a cauldron now properly places a powder snow cauldron in all cases.
* Added block tag `ceramics:extra_bucket_blocks`. Any blocks added to this tag can be picked up and placed using a clay bucket.
* Fix creative not showing solid clay buckets (e.g. powder snow). The bucket was shown in JEI due to some legacy code so this bug was missed before.
* Fix cracked empty clay buckets not having a translation key.
* Fix cracked clay buckets not always showing the "cracked" tooltip.
* Fix powder snow fluids tagged `forge:powder_snow` not working with the powder snow clay bucket.
* Fix milk clay bucket not having capability by @VoidLeech in https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/pull/88

## Fluid transfer

* Added all gauges to the cistern connections tag.
* Added recipe builder for clay repair recipes. This replaces the old finished recipe, though I suspect no one was using that (and it only breaks datagen).
* Prevent flowing liquids from breaking porcelain channels and faucets. Opted to keep the behavior where it breaks clay channels and faucets.
* Fix faucets getting stuck when pouring into a tank that does not support at least 25mb increments.
* Fix several bugs with cisterns having the wrong tank size on the client after breaking or placing extensions.
* Fix channels, faucets, and cisterns not always calling `setChanged` when their state changed, potentially causing fluid deletion.

## Kiln

* Added recipe book support to the kiln.
* Show fuels in the fuel slot for the kiln JEI support.
* Kiln recipes now use Mantle's `ItemOutput`, meaning they can output a tag instead of just a value.
* Added a kiln recipe builder compared to using the vanilla builder. Makes it easier to add kiln recipes and furnace recipes together.

## Bricks

* Make dragon bricks show at a luminosity of 7, regardless of light level.
* Make the lava part of lava bricks show at a luminosity of 14, regardless of light level.
* Move render types to model JSON. This should allow models a bit more control but may cause resource packs changing the gauges to need an update.


## Translations
* Czech localisation for Ceramics [COMPLETE] by @RomanPlayer22 in https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/pull/87
* Update some outdated lang keys to the newest keys, should add better support for the less recently updated translations.

## New Contributors
* @RomanPlayer22 made their first contribution in https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/pull/87
* @VoidLeech made their first contribution in https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/pull/88

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/compare/v1.8.0...v1.8.1

releases.notes:
## Gameplay

* Gauges now show tooltips of fluid contents looking directly at them.
* Kilns are now crafted using terracotta instead of clay bricks.
* Channels now have slightly more internal capacity to support intersecting channels in some circumstances.
* Gauges are now easier to place on channels.
* Gauges on channels no longer shows the amount of fluid, as that's not properly synced to client.

## Data packs

* Added fluid tag `ceramics:bucket_blacklist` to prevent a fluid from working in clay buckets. By default, this includes potions.
* Added fluid tag `ceramics:hide_in_bucket` tag, to prevent a fluid from showing in JEI but still allow it to work. Notably used for a couple of fluids that have another bucket variant such as powdered snow.

## Resource packs

* Migrated to the new Mantle systems for block entity renderer data in resource packs. Look under `assets/ceramics/` to configure models.
* Fix invalid newline characters in some item tooltips.

## Compatibility

* Migrated to the gauge code from Mantle.
* Updated kiln support in JEI.
* Use Mantle's fluid transfer helper to allow storing weird fluid items such as water bottles in cisterns. Things like potions and soup also work if any mod adds a fluid to the proper tag.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KnightMiner/Ceramics/compare/v1.7.1...v1.8.0

* Fix broken terracotta cisterns, faucets, and channels not stacking with freshly crafted ones

Language
* Added Simplified Chinese Translation (thanks Aemande123)

mods.name: Ceramics
mods.description: Mod adding additional early game and vanilla-like tools made of clay. Includes fluid transport, decoration, and ceramic tools.

releases.notes:
**Added**

Terracotta and porcelain blocks
* All fluid blocks come in terracotta and porcelain variants
* Terracotta does not hold hot fluids well, and will crack over time, eventually breaking. Cracked terracotta can be repaired with raw clay
* Porcelain is heat resistant, but requires quartz to craft.
* Additionally, all blocks are available in raw clay and porcelain variants. These can be placed in world, but serve no functionality.

Cisterns
* Cisterns are the updated barrels from 1.12.
* Instead of crafting extensions and bases separately, cisterns automatically connect to the same color below
* Can hold 4 buckets for terracotta, or 6 for porcelain
* Visually connect to faucets, channels, and gauges.

Gauges
* New block to check the fluid level of a fluid tank such as a cistern
* When right clicked, displays the fluid name and the fluid level of the adjacent tank

Faucets
* Ported from 1.12
* Move fluids from the side or bottom of a block into the block below
* Improved redstone interactions over 1.12, should also be more efficient

Channels
* Ported from 1.12.
* Filled with faucets, pour fluid into adjacent or below blocks.
* Can interact to change connections
* More efficient than the 1.12 version.

**Changed**

* All fired clay items are now called "Terracotta" for consistency with vanilla.
* Raw clay is universally named "Clay"
* Fired porcelain is called "Porcelain", while unfired will be "Unfired Porcelain" or simply "Unfired"
* Updated dragon bricks textures for 1.16. They were the one variant that never got a texture update.
